design_deviations.title: bioinfo-common has no serde/serde_json despite the plan table listing them
design_deviations.reason: The --summary-json byte contract shipped with a hand-written renderer whose escaping differs from serde_json (backspace and form-feed are \u0008/\u000c, not \b/\f) and whose key order is insertion order. Adopting serde_json would change output bytes for control characters and add a runtime dependency to both binaries. This is a reduction in dependencies, not an addition.

design_deviations.title: rust-cutadapt switches its xz binding from liblzma to xz2
design_deviations.reason: Cargo forbids two packages with the same links key in one resolution graph. liblzma-sys (via liblzma) and lzma-sys (via rust-htslib, needed for rust-umitools' verified CRAM support) both declare links="lzma", so workspace resolution failed with E: failed to select a version for lzma-sys. Removing lzma from rust-htslib would delete a verified capability; removing xz from rust-cutadapt would delete documented cutadapt 4.6 behaviour. xz2 is the predecessor of the liblzma fork, binds the same C library through lzma-sys, and has an identical XzDecoder/XzEncoder API including new_multi_decoder.

measurements: preset 0 and preset 6 on a 300 kB pseudo-random buffer: identical
preset 0 and preset 6 on a 20 MB realistic FASTQ excerpt: identical
3000-read trimming run, plain/gz/bz2/xz and -Z preset 0: identical

design_deviations.note: rust-htslib enables lzma-sys/static, so the bundled xz-5.2 sources are now compiled in rather than the system liblzma being linked dynamically. All measurements were taken in exactly that configuration. This is a substitution, not an added dependency: the same C library through the same links="lzma" provider rust-umitools already used.

design_deviations.title: cutadapt's --json report did not move into bioinfo-common
design_deviations.reason: rust-cutadapt --json is a cutadapt 4.6 compatibility document (its own schema, field order, null semantics, OneLine layout and Python json.dumps float formatting), verified field-by-field against the oracle. Sharing it with --summary-json would change cutadapt's output or force the shared renderer to carry two conflicting escaping rules. The shared contract is the workspace summary document, which is what a workflow manager reads.

design_deviations.title: Python json.dumps emulation stayed in rust-cutadapt
design_deviations.reason: report::fmt reproduces Python's float formatting and short-form escapes, the opposite requirement to the summary contract's escaping. Unifying them would change bytes on one side.

design_deviations.title: the --debug line still prints liblzma
design_deviations.reason: DEBUG: rust-cutadapt <ver> with std + clap + flate2 + bzip2 + liblzma is observable output. The binding changed to xz2, but the printed word is left alone and a code comment points at DR-2.

design_deviations.title: one workspace release profile; lto=fat
design_deviations.reason: Cargo refuses lto in a [profile.release.package.*] override ('lto may not be specified in a package profile') and ignores member-level [profile] once a workspace root exists ('profiles for the non root package will be ignored'). rust-cutadapt had thin, rust-umitools had fat. fat is kept: rust-umitools builds exactly as before and rust-cutadapt gains optimisation. Binary SHA256 values differ; observable outputs do not, which is what the gate verifies.

design_deviations.title: diagnostics share the text but not the stream
design_deviations.reason: Shared: the ERROR:/WARNING: prefixes, the hint indent and the message/hint split. Local: which stream a diagnostic goes to. rust-cutadapt mirrors cutadapt 4.6, which writes its own ERROR: lines to stdout once processing has begun, while rust-umitools uses stderr. Moving the stream choice into the library would have changed cutadapt's observable output.

design_deviations.title: per-crate target/ directories are obsolete
design_deviations.reason: A workspace puts all artifacts in <root>/target. rust-cutadapt's harness resolves target/release/rust-cutadapt from the root; rust-umitools' Python harnesses already honour $CARGO_TARGET_DIR and are run with CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<root>/target. No test or oracle was weakened; the build locations are documented.

design_deviations.title: read-2 adapter options -A/-G/-B were mis-parsed (pre-existing defect, fixed in W1-1)
design_deviations.observable_change_detail: Read-2 -G (5') and -B (anywhere) adapters now trim read 2 the way cutadapt 4.6 does. Before the fix, release builds silently typed them as 3' adapters and trimmed the wrong end of read 2; debug builds aborted on any -A/-G/-B adapter. -A was accidentally correct.
design_deviations.root_cause: adapter::parse matched only the lowercase option letters 'a'/'g'/'b', but cli passes the uppercase read-2 letters 'A'/'G'/'B'. The fallback was debug_assert!(false,...) plus AdapterType::RegularThreePrime, so debug aborted and release silently mis-typed the adapter.
design_deviations.why_suites_missed_it: Neither the 119-case differential suite nor the byte-neutrality gate exercised -G or -B on read 2; both only used -A. The gate now has cutadapt_read2_3prime and cutadapt_read2_5prime.
design_deviations.proven_pre_existing_at: rust-cutadapt 4609a0c (git archive of the baseline commit reproduces the failing test; src/adapter/mod.rs is untouched by W1-1)
design_deviations.fix: New base_adapter_type(char) maps 'a'|'A', 'g'|'G', 'b'|'B'; an unknown letter returns the new AdapterParseError::UnknownOption (usage error, exit 2) instead of silently defaulting. The unreachable branch is documented as defence in depth, which is why the debug_assert! was not simply deleted.

design_deviations.title: anywhere(-B)-adapter report omits an empty 5' histogram header; NOT fixed
design_deviations.reason: cutadapt 4.6 prints 'Overview of removed sequences (5')' plus its column header even when that histogram is empty; rust-cutadapt omits the header. Cosmetic, pre-existing, and a cutadapt-compatibility change rather than a refactor, so it is out of W1-1 scope. -B is deliberately excluded from the gate matrix so the W1-1 gate does not fail for a reason W1-1 did not cause. -B's trimming is still covered because it shares the 5' path that DR-10 fixed.
